faq.question: How much does window replacement cost in East Palo Alto?
faq.answer: East Palo Alto homeowners typically invest $4,500 to $10,000 for a full window replacement project covering 8–12 windows. This compact Peninsula community's older 1960s–1980s homes offer excellent value for full-home replacement projects. Single window installation starts at approximately $450.

faq.question: Do I need a permit to replace windows in East Palo Alto?
faq.answer: Yes. East Palo Alto requires a building permit for window replacement. Our team handles all permit applications with the City of East Palo Alto Building Department on your behalf.

faq.question: Is it worth replacing 20-year-old windows in East Palo Alto?
faq.answer: Often yes. Twenty-year-old windows in East Palo Alto commonly show fogged glass, drafts and weak locks. Newer ENERGY STAR units improve comfort and curb appeal; Deluxe Windows compares payback against your utility rates and home style before recommending replacement.

faq.question: Should I choose fiberglass or vinyl windows in East Palo Alto?
faq.answer: Vinyl is the value pick for most East Palo Alto replacements and handles Bay Area weather well. Fiberglass (including Marvin Ultrex) is stronger, more stable in temperature swings and better for larger openings or coastal exposure. We show both side by side in the showroom and on-site.

faq.question: How long does window replacement take in East Palo Alto?
faq.answer: Most East Palo Alto projects are measured in one visit and installed in one to three working days once products arrive — typically four to eight weeks after ordering, depending on brand and custom sizes.
